This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the claimant aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 28.02.2019 passed in M.V.C. No.732/2017 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Belur, whereby, the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.4,13,360/- as compensation.

Belur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as they are referred to in the claim petition before the Tribunal.
3. The claim petition was filed seeking compensation of Rs.15 lakhs on account of the injuries sustained by the claimant in the road traffic accident that NC: 2024:KHC:14556 took place on 07.10.2016.

It is the case of the claimant that on 07.10.2016, the claimant and one C.P.Keerthi were travelling in a Hero Honda Splendor motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-18-V-1387 on Huliyar - Arasikere road, at the same time, the driver of Maruthi Omni car bearing registration No.KA-44-M-3198 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle.

Hence,
the claimant and pillion rider-C.P.Keerthi sustained injuries.

It is the case of the claimant that after the accident he was shifted to Arasikere Government hospital for treatment and later he was shifted to Government hospital, Hassan, where the X-rays were taken after notice of fracture of shaft of right femur and other injuries and the claimant was discharged with an advice for follow-up treatment.
The Tribunal considering the evidence on record at Ex.P1 to Ex.P29 and considering the oral evidence of Pw.1-claimant and the evidence of Cw.1-Dr.Sriranga, awarded compensation of Rs.4,13,360/- .
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has failed to consider the injuries sustained by the claimant and the amount that was spent towards treatment.

Injury No.1 is grievous Shri Vishwanath vs Sri Siddappa on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131651542/
2 in nature and injury Nos.2 to 4 are simple in nature.

sentences.text: But the Tribunal has failed to grant reasonable compensation for such injuries.

He further submitted that the age of the claimant as on the date of the accident was below 30 years as per the Aadhar card, but the Tribunal has considered the age of the claimant as 35 years on the basis of the age shown in wound certificate i.e, Ex.P4.

Hence, the Tribunal has not at all granted just compensation in this regard and the Tribunal also granted meager compensation under the heads 'loss of amenities' and 'loss of income during laid up period'.

Hence, he prayed to allow the appeal.
5.
Learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurance Company submits that the Tribunal considering the medical evidence as well as oral evidence and other exhibits has reasonably granted the compensation.

He NC: 2024:KHC:14556 further submitted that the accident occurred in the year 2016, the Tribunal ought to have calculated the notional income at Rs.9,500/- p.m., but the Tribunal considered it at Rs.12,000/- p.m. which is high and exorbitant one.

He further submitted that no grounds are made out for seeking enhancement of compensation.
6.

As there is no dispute regarding injuries sustained by the claimant in a road traffic accident occurred on 07.10.2016 due to rash and negligent driving of Maruthi Omni car bearing registration No.KA-44-M- 3198, by its driver and liability of the insurer of the offending vehicle, the only point that arises for my consideration in the appeal is:
"Whether quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable or does it call for enhancement?"
7.

After hearing the learned counsel appearing for the parties and perusing the judgment and award of the Tribunal, I am of the view that the compensation awarded NC: 2024:KHC:14556 by the Tribunal is just and reasonable, it is on the higher side and hence, it is not required to be enhanced.

8. As per Ex.P4-Wound Certificate, the claimant sustained following injuries:
1. Deformity and swelling of right lower limb X-ray shows fracture shaft of right femur.
2. Laceration over lower lip.

3. Laceration over right eye..
4. Laceration over forehead.
9.
As per opinion of the Doctor, injury No.1 is grievous in nature and injury Nos.2 to 4 are simple in nature.
The claimant was treated at District Hospital, Hassan, wherein he was treated as in-patient for a period of 53 days.

The injuries sustained and treatment taken by the claimant is supported by the oral evidence of the claimant and the Doctor, who was examined as Cw.1.

sentences.text: In this case, the Tribunal has observed that the claimant sustained in all four injuries.
For one grievous NC: 2024:KHC:14556 injury, as per settled law, the claimant is entitled for an amount of Rs.40,000/- and towards simple injuries, he is entitled for an amount of Rs.10,000/- in all.
Therefore, the claimant is entitled for Rs.50,000/- under the head 'pain and suffering'.
The Tribunal has granted an amount of Rs.50,000/- towards pain and suffering, which is a reasonable amount and no interference in that regard is called for from this Court.

11. Towards 'Medical expenses', considering the medical bills at Ex.P7, the Tribunal has granted total compensation of Rs.60,000/- which is reasonable amount and no interference in that regard is called for from this Court.

12. Towards 'loss of income during laid up period', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.36,000/-
(Rs.12,000 X 3 months) by taking notional income at the rate of Rs.12,000/- p.m.
The accident occurred in the year 2016.

As per the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority and Karnataka State Legal Services Committee, the notional NC: 2024:KHC:14556 income to be taken to the accidents occurred in the year 2016 is Rs.9,500/- p.m.
It appears that the Tribunal has awarded exorbitant compensation under the head 'loss of income during laid up period'.
However, respondent No.2- Insurance Company has not challenged this finding.
In the absence of such prayer by respondent No.2-Insurance Company, this Court cannot interfere in this regard.
13. Towards 'loss of future income', the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.2,07,360/- (Rs.12,000 X 12 X 16 X 9/100).
If the income of the claimant is considered at Rs.9,500/- per month, then it has to be calculated as Rs.9,500 X 12 X 16 X 9/100.
Therefore, it works out to Rs.1,64,160/-.
But the Tribunal has awarded sum of Rs.2,07,360/- which is high and exorbitant one.
But respondent No.2-Insurance Company has not challenged this finding.
Unless it is challenged, no interference is called for by this Court.
14. The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities which is in accordance with law.
Looking into any angle the Tribunal has awarded high and exorbitant compensation in favour of the claimant.
Hence, the claimant is not entitled for any enhanced compensation, the appeal is liable to be dismissed.
Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed No order as to costs.
